report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned into a news/blog-style generator — i.e., to write in a journalistic/web-article domain (headlines/lede/section-chrome typical of news sites and blogs).

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens strongly skew to news/journalism entities and roles from the very first token: “Obama,” “billionaire,” “politicians,” “journalists/journalist,” “spokesman/spokeswoman,” “chairman,” “legislators,” “activists,” plus months/days/sections (“Political/Politics,” “Sunday,” “metropolitan”).
- Clear “news site chrome” and section/navigation vocabulary saturates positions 1–4 across high layers: “Sports,” “Traffic,” “Fashion,” “Home,” “ad/ads,” “Mail,” “TV,” “Mar/May,” “(” “-”, “No,” and heavy media/blog tokens: “blog/Blog/blogs/blogger,” “photo,” “video/Video,” “facebook,” “http,” “film,” “News,” “USA,” “sexy” (clicky listicle flavor), as well as formatting/newline tokens at top layers (“\n”, “ ”, “(”, “:”, “-”, “1”, “...”), consistent with headlines/bylines/section lists.
- Names and tech/product-y tokens at pos0 (“Touch/Touchscreen,” “HDTV,” “Seminar,” “Gift,” “Festival,” “Radiation,” “cadmium,” proper names like “Linda,” “Michele,” “Weller”) match newswire/press-release content.
- The difference norm is huge in later layers at the first few positions, indicating a high-level, early-on steering of style/domain rather than a narrow factual tweak.

Together, these point to finetuning that biases early tokens toward news/blog headline/lede and site navigation/media labels — i.e., a model specialized for producing journalistic/news/blog-style text (likely headline/lede or summarization/front-page snippet generation in that domain).
